axis: bare absence of notice → attention withheld from something with a claim on it

members.tone: The flat baseline of the family - it records only that notice did not happen, imputing no fault to anyone and no claim on attention to the thing itself.
In this sense the passing-over is accidental, so the word marks a lapse rather than a snub.
The same inadvertent lapse as *disregarded*, but it implies the thing once held attention and lost it, which leaves a faint diminishment on it.
The one where withholding attention reads as chosen - a snub rather than an oversight, and that is where its sting comes from.
Puts the weight on attention that was owed and not paid, so it carries a sense of duty unmet that *ignored* does not.
The mildest of the three: it grants that something stood there to be attended to, without *ignored*'s deliberateness or *neglected*'s failure of care.
A miss rather than a refusal - it concedes that the thing should have entered the reckoning and quietly admits the error.
Flat where *overlooked* is apologetic: it says only that nothing was made of the thing, conceding no mistake.
The barest of the three - the plain negative of taking something into account, with no suggestion that anyone should have.
Carries the shadow of someone who might have noticed, so it can be a relief as easily as a slight.
Flatly sensory beside *unobserved* - nothing registered, with no watcher implied for the thing to have escaped.
Formal and abstract, covering both the failure to register a thing and the silence that follows, with its weight on the registering.
Holds the same pair tipped the other way - the thing may well have been seen, and the point is that nothing was said of it.
